name: Itopride

overview.mechanism: Combines dopamine D2 receptor antagonism with acetylcholinesterase inhibition. [[ITO-EARLY,ITO-P3]]
uses: Studied for symptomatic functional dyspepsia; verify the local product’s approved indication. [[ITO-EARLY,ITO-P3]]

paragraphs.text: An eight-week placebo-controlled trial randomized 554 patients. Among those with outcome data, symptom-free or markedly improved status was more frequent in the itopride groups than placebo. This early positive study assessed dyspepsia symptoms rather than kidney outcomes.

Two subsequent phase 3 trials did not reproduce a benefit on global patient response: rates were 45.2% versus 45.6% in one trial and 37.8% versus 35.4% in the other. One symptom-questionnaire endpoint favored itopride in the international trial but not the North American trial. The evidence therefore does not justify an unqualified claim of consistent superiority to placebo.

Overall trial tolerability resembled placebo, but prolactin elevations were more frequent with itopride (18/579 versus 1/591). These short-term findings do not establish safety during prolonged therapy or in advanced CKD. The cited dyspepsia studies provide no dialysis dosing regimen; consult product-specific renal prescribing information.

sources.citation: A placebo-controlled trial of itopride in functional dyspepsia. PubMed PMID: 16495395.
